main_body: Japanese storehouse-style building: slate tile roof with a ridge band, white plaster band, a lower roof, and a dark wooden lattice front with a door opening and straw bundles at the base
top_band: Ridge cap rows 1-5 (L 158/130/83) with a dark edge at row 6; below it a large sloped tile roof rows 7-32 (L about 130 to 56) that reads as a roof surface above the front walls
evidence: Column x=32 reads as ridge cap (rows 1-5), a dark step at row 6, and a tall tile roof slope (rows 7-32) that overhangs a dark eave row (30-32). A cream plaster band (rows 33-40) and a second smaller roof (41-47) follow. Below them is the wall with a dark door recess (rows 50-76) and inset lattice. Both roofs show as sloped surfaces above vertical faces, with eave shadows and an inset door, so the building holds together as a roofed 3/4 structure. The roof is drawn with vertical tile lines and not much foreshortening, which makes it borderline.

style.evidence: The candidate is far below both references on measured facts: 7 colours per tile against 18 and 11, and 33 distinct colours against 185 and 66. 72% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline is mostly a neutral dark line and not a tinted material tone. The roof has regular vertical tile stripes with only about 4 slate steps. It has no per-tile scallops or highlights, and the plaster band and dark door area are flat and plain. The lattice and straw add some texture, but overall it is thinner and more sticker-like than the references.
